Command: Offer a guilt offering for misappropriation of holy things
Summary: The command: Offer a guilt offering for misappropriation of holy things (Leviticus 5:15). One who sinned through ignorance against the holy things of the LORD brought a ram without blemish, with restitution plus a fifth.
Commandment: Offer a guilt offering for misappropriation of holy things, as prescribed in Leviticus 5:15.
Application: This row narrows the parent group command to this one mitzvah. The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. Hebrews teaches these sacrifices could never perfect the worshiper; they pointed forward to Christ's once-for-all offering, which is why they ceased with the new covenant.
Purpose: To provide atonement, thanksgiving, and fellowship under the old covenant. Hebrews teaches these pointed forward to Christ's once-for-all offering (Hebrews 10:1-14), so the system ceased.
Function: One who sinned against the holy things brought a ram, with restitution plus a fifth — a ceremonial law of atonement and repayment. Its goal was to set right a wrong done to God's own things: the holy could not be used carelessly and left unmended. The evil was misappropriation of what belonged to the LORD, treating holy things as common property. It restrained that evil twice over — the offering atoned, and the extra fifth made the thief pay back more than he took.
